name: Skitgubbe
description: Skitgubbe (Swedish: 'Shit Old Man', also known simply as 'Skit' or 'Mattis') is a traditional Swedish card game for 3 players. It is divided into two distinct phases: Phase 1 (Trick-Taking/Collection) where players try to gather good cards, and Phase 2 (Shedding/Battle) where the goal is to get rid of all cards. The loser is the last player holding cards and is declared the 'Skitgubbe'.
deck: Standard 52-card pack without joker. Three cards each; remainder forms the stock. Rank A (high) down to 2 (low).

history.origins: Dates back to the 19th century in rural Sweden. Related to Finnish 'Paskahousu' (Shit Pants).
timeline: 1950s: Rules formalized as 'Mattis' in some regions.
Present: Still popular among students and families.
history.cultural: Being the Skitgubbe carries a mild social stigma or requires buying the next round.
history.evolution: The two-phase structure makes it unique; Phase 1 is purely preparatory for Phase 2.

setup.players: Two to four players; best for three.
setup.dealing: Deal three cards to each player clockwise, starting with forehand. Place the remainder face down as the stock (talon).

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player with cards in phase 2; the last player left with cards is the loser (the skitgubbe).
rules.gameplay: Two phases. Phase 1: Two-player tricks; player to dealer's left leads, next player plays; higher card wins; no follow suit; after playing, each draws from stock to keep three cards. Equal cards (stunsa): cards stay, both draw, same leader leads again. Option: turn up top card of stock and play it. Last card of stock sets trump for phase 2. Phase 2: Player who drew trump leads; must beat previous card (higher same suit or any trump) or pick it up; trick complete when as many cards as active players; completer leads next or player to left if out.
keyRules: Phase 1: Two-card tricks, higher rank wins, draw from stock after playing.
Phase 2: Beat or pick up; follow suit when beating; trump beats non-trump.
Last card of stock determines trump; holder leads phase 2.

strategy.basic: In Phase 1, throw away your low cards (Trash). Keep your Aces and 10s. Do not win tricks that contain low cards unless you have to (Phase 1 tricks go into your hand for Phase 2? Yes! You collect the trick). So, you want to win tricks with high cards inside them. Losing a trick means you don't get the cards. But you want high cards. So win big tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Counting Suits: In Phase 2, you must follow suit. If you have the only Spade left (the Ace), hold it until someone leads Spades, then crush them. If you have small cards in Phase 2, try to sneak them out early or on a new lead.
strategy.advanced: The 'Sacrifice': Sometimes in Phase 1, you let an opponent win a trick full of Queens if it means you can save your Ace for a trick full of Aces/Kings later. The quality of your Phase 2 hand is everything.
tips: Don't hoard one suit in Phase 1—diversity helps in Phase 2.
The last trick of Phase 1 is crucial for lead control.

variations.name: All play to each trick (phase 1)
variations.description: In phase 1 all players play to each trick; highest rank wins; ties resolved by replay. Can use sluffing. Often played 2–6 players.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes phase 1 participation only; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Mas with turned up trump
variations.description: Trump turned up after deal; phase 1 beat by higher led suit or trump. Player with three trumps may store them and draw three new; two of trumps may exchange for turnup.
